links.summary: Two independent ways the same retention value goes wrong: the UI writes it late and reads it once, and the backend parser clamps anything it cannot parse instead of reporting it.
Same failure mode, different cause: one assertion cannot fail because its expected value is derived from the subject, the other cannot fail because an empty input makes both sides zero.
Both are properties of the same fuzzyRouteMatcher route table: a guard that cannot see its own phantom entry, and a suggestion ranking whose ties are settled by array position.
The miscount that made the label wrong, and the aggregate invariant that was satisfied the whole time and therefore could not report it.
The remedy for the mislabelled bucket: a property-level rule, so the classification survives the next file that uses the same unscaled property.
The rule has to live in two places that a later session will read differently: the code that classifies, and the evidence string that describes it.
Adding a fifth bucket while every existing name is frozen, and the sum that the new key has to join for --verify to have any purchase.
Both are host-specific audit invariants carried as a standing constraint on the same script, one about the shell toolchain and one about the output contract.
Two ways a review of tests goes wrong: anchoring the numbers to a tree that was still moving, and trusting an assertion that was computed from its own subject.
